headline: Man Utd sack Carrick during the break and hand Pochettino a 2.5-year deal for an Anfield debut
facts: United waited for the November international break after the 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth on 25 October before sacking Michael Carrick and appointing Mauricio Pochettino.
Pochettino's first match is away at Liverpool on Sunday 22 November, with United 18th in the Premier League table.
ESPN reports the deal runs about two and a half years, to 2029; the exact appointment date is not stated in the sources, so 17 Nov is approximate.
background: Carrick took United to third place and Champions League qualification last season, per CEO Omar Berrada; Pochettino previously managed Tottenham from 2014 and was sacked there in November 2019.
footage_terms: Pochettino first press conference Manchester United

headline: Man Utd 4-4 Aston Villa: twice two goals down, equaliser in the 97th minute
facts: Villa led 2-0 inside four minutes through Alysson and Nicolas Jackson, a club-record concession of two goals in 3 minutes 42 seconds for United.
United came back twice: Bruno Fernandes scored a penalty, Zirkzee pulled one back in stoppage time, and substitute Patrick Dorgu equalised in the 97th minute from a Fernandes corner.

Fans called on the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe to sell, and United stayed 18th, winless in eight league games. Emery stormed off after the equaliser and sarcastically asked a reporter if there would be 'more questions'.
background: Emery's Villa were sixth in the Champions League table before this match; United's Carrick was sacked about a week later.
footage_terms: Dorgu equaliser Aston Villa Old Trafford
Emery post match interview Manchester United draw
Man Utd Villa 4-4 fans protest Glazers

headline: Drone operator films Pochettino's first Man Utd training session, posts 12 minutes online
facts: A roughly 12-minute drone video of Pochettino's first Carrington training session was posted on YouTube by an operator who runs the CC Overview channel.
The operator has since removed it and apologised, calling it a serious error of judgment and saying the flight was legal but filming was unethical.
Sky reports United will not take legal action this time but could if it happens again; Liverpool boss Iraola said the footage should not be legal.
background: United meet Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday 22 November, which is Pochettino's first match in charge.

headline: Berrada: Fernandes has turned down two contract offers, Pochettino says he stays captain
facts: Sky Sports News reported that Bruno Fernandes has rejected two contract offers and his deal expires at the end of this season; Berrada said talks continue privately.
Pochettino said Fernandes is the captain and a very important player, and deferred questions on a new contract.
ESPN notes United hold an option for a one-year extension to 2028, and that Fernandes had criticised Carrick's tactics in Carrick's final weeks.
background: Fernandes is 32, has been United's captain and top performer, and was ranked No. 1 in Sky Sports' Premier League top 25 in March before sliding to 11th.

headline: Bruno Fernandes falls from No. 1 to 11th in Sky Sports' Premier League top 25
facts: Erling Haaland is now No. 1 in the Sky Sports ranking, up from fourth in March.
Fernandes was No. 1 in March and has dropped 10 places to 11th; he is the only United player in the top 25.
No player from Tottenham, Newcastle or Aston Villa appears in the top 25.
background: Fernandes is United's captain and the club's best player but his contract runs out at the end of the season.
footage_terms: Bruno Fernandes best Premier League player

headline: Berrada admits third coach in under three seasons, 18th place 'unacceptable', £163m spent in summer
facts: Berrada said three permanent managers in less than three seasons (ten Hag, Amorim, Carrick) shows instability, and the third straight season with a mid-season coach change.
United spent £163m this summer, mainly on midfielders Baleba, Tielemans and Santos; Berrada said a left-back like Newcastle's Lewis Hall was considered but not chased at inflated prices.
He said the Glazer and INEOS co-ownership is working well, and that he had no involvement in Manchester City's alleged wrongdoing from his time there.
background: Berrada was chief operating officer at Manchester City from 2016 and worked at City Football Group until 2024 before joining United.

headline: Pochettino squad audit: Rashford on £325k a week, Mount with four full league games since 2023
facts: ESPN's Mark Ogden puts Fernandes and Rashford (29, highest earner at £325,000 a week) in the 'go' column; United failed to move Rashford in the last two summers after loans to Aston Villa and Barcelona.
Mount is on contract until 2028 and has completed four 90-minute Premier League games since 2023 with 71 games missed to injury; De Ligt has 343 days out injured since his €45m signing in 2024.
Sesko (€85m) is described as unlikely to recoup his fee; Shaw and Martinez are both out of contract soon.
background: Pochettino inherited a squad built by six previous managers, going back to Louis van Gaal's signing of Luke Shaw in 2014.

headline: JJ Gabriel, 16, leaving Man Utd amid Real Madrid interest, club annoyed at how he announced it
facts: Berrada said the 16-year-old JJ Gabriel is leaving United amid interest from Real Madrid.
He said the club was unhappy that the player announced his departure without informing United first.
background: United have a history of losing top academy teenagers to bigger clubs, and Berrada is the CEO trying to stabilise recruitment.

headline: Bournemouth win 3-0 at Old Trafford, United's eighth league game without a win
facts: Bournemouth scored through Rayan (38'), Marcus Tavernier (43') and Evanilson (71') at Old Trafford.
The result dropped United to 16th and extended the winless run to eight league games.
The match report calls United lifeless; pressure on Michael Carrick grew sharply afterwards.
background: Carrick, appointed to replace Ruben Amorim, had taken United to third place the season before.

headline: Chelsea 2-0 Man Utd: Lisandro Martinez sent off, nine league and cup games without a win
facts: Morgan Rogers scored in the 50th minute and Cole Palmer converted a penalty in the 64th at Stamford Bridge.
Lisandro Martinez was sent off for a second yellow, the booking coming for conceding the penalty.
United's winless run reached nine matches and Carrick's job was reported to be under pressure.
background: Martinez is in the final year of his United contract, with a 12-month option, according to Sky Sports.

headline: United come from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2: Cunha scores twice and is sent off
facts: Roma led 2-0 by the 18th minute through Soule and a Malen penalty.
Bruno Fernandes scored a penalty on the retake after the first was saved, then Matheus Cunha scored in the 83rd and 86th minutes.
Cunha was sent off for a second yellow in stoppage time; the win ended a nine-match winless run for United.
background: Cunha joined United in 2025 for £62.5m and has 14 goals since arriving, per ESPN's squad audit.
footage_terms: Cunha two goals Roma Champions League

headline: Spurs and United draw 1-1: Bentancur red-carded for headbutting Luke Shaw, Solanke equalises in added time
facts: Bryan Mbeumo put United ahead in the 73rd minute; Dominic Solanke headed an equaliser at 90+2.
Rodrigo Bentancur was sent off about 12 minutes after coming on for headbutting Luke Shaw.
It was Tottenham's first point of the season from a draw and left United with 6 points. The page's shot map conflicts on scorers, so details are from the scoreboard and commentary.
background: Spurs beat United in the 2025 Europa League final.
footage_terms: Bentancur red card Luke Shaw headbutt

headline: Osimhen reportedly on Man Utd's radar for January under Pochettino, but no release clause
facts: Goal, citing The Sun and Turkish sources, says United are interested again and Osimhen would accept wages close to his current deal.
Osimhen is 27 and under contract at Galatasaray until June 2029 with no release clause; Turkish sources value him at £80m to £100m.
Sesko and Zirkzee have scored four goals combined this season. Neither club has confirmed talks.
background: Osimhen scored 37 goals in his first season after joining Galatasaray permanently and 22 the following season.

headline: Hurzeler says he is staying at Brighton after Man Utd rumours; Tony Bloom vows to keep him
facts: Reports said United had considered Hurzeler as a replacement for the sacked Michael Carrick before appointing Pochettino.
Hurzeler called the links just rumours and said he is fully committed to Brighton.
Brighton are second in the Premier League and Tony Bloom said he would fight hard to keep him.
background: Brighton are second in the table while United sit 18th.

headline: Mudryk's viral podcast: Arsenal was the club he wanted, now on loan at Spurs
facts: On the Guest of Gordon podcast, Mudryk said Arsenal were the club he wanted to play for in 2023 and a move to the Emirates was his dream.
Mudryk is on loan at Spurs from Chelsea, has played only 16 minutes since arriving on deadline day and has been out with an ankle injury since September.
De Zerbi said he understands fan frustration, defended Mudryk, sidestepped a question about cancelling the loan, and said the winger is two to three weeks from training.
background: Mudryk, 25, moved to Chelsea in 2023 after being close to joining Arsenal, and has served a drugs ban.
footage_terms: Mudryk Tottenham De Zerbi press conference
Mudryk Arsenal podcast Guest of Gordon

headline: Thomas Frank unveiled at Crystal Palace, jokes about the Arsenal coffee cup that haunted his Spurs spell
facts: Frank, 53, took over bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace on a contract to June 2029, with a first game away at Coventry.
In January, as Spurs manager, he was photographed with an Arsenal-branded cup before a loss to Bournemouth; he now says he hopes not to be pictured with another rival's cup.
He was sacked by Spurs in February after just under eight months and hinted there is more to tell about that spell one day.
background: Frank had stabilised Brentford in the Premier League and was nominated for Manager of the Year there before moving to Spurs.
footage_terms: Thomas Frank Crystal Palace press conference

headline: Spurs beat Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, first win there since 2018, Palmer sent off
facts: Chelsea keeper Mike Penders punched a corner into his own net in the 77th minute and Mathys Tel added a solo goal in the 87th.
Cole Palmer was sent off for a second yellow card.
It was Tottenham's first win at Stamford Bridge since April 2018 and Chelsea's first home league defeat under Xabi Alonso, per the commentary.
background: Spurs had been bottom of the table before their first league win on 19 October.

headline: Spurs finally win a league game: 3-1 over Coventry lifts them off the bottom
facts: James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies (90+6') scored for Spurs; Jack Rudoni replied for Coventry.
It was Tottenham's first Premier League win of the season and moved them off the bottom of the table.
Spurs had 65% possession and five shots on target to Coventry's one.
background: De Zerbi arrived at Spurs after the club had faced relegation last season, and Spurs spent over £330m this summer, per Sky Sports.

headline: Spurs beat Palace 2-0 as Mateta is sent off; third straight league win, first in about 20 months
facts: Archie Gray headed in a corner in the 25th minute and Jan Paul van Hecke added a second in the 73rd.
Mateta was sent off for a late lunge on Micky van de Ven after VAR upgraded a yellow card.
Spurs had 34 shots to Palace's 2 and moved up to eighth place.
background: Palace sit in the relegation zone and have now turned to Thomas Frank, who was sacked by Spurs in February.
footage_terms: Mateta red card Van de Ven

headline: Leeds 1-0 Spurs: Okafor's late goal ends Leeds' five-game winless run
facts: Substitute Noah Okafor scored in the 79th minute at Elland Road.
Spurs had about 61% possession but lower expected goals (roughly 0.7 against about 2.0 for Leeds).
It was only the second Leeds win in 14 Premier League meetings between the clubs.
background: Spurs host Ipswich on 21 November and sit 11th on 12 points.

headline: Xavi Simons ahead of schedule in ACL recovery, eyeing a return around the end of January
facts: Simons tore his anterior cruciate ligament on 25 April in Tottenham's 1-0 win at Wolves, which ruled him out of the last four league games and the World Cup.
He expects to start phase three of rehab later in November, which would bring him back into team training.
A competitive return around the nine-month mark, near the end of January, is possible.
background: Spurs are 11th and have scored fewer goals than all but two Premier League sides after 10 matches, per Sky Sports.

headline: Spurs spent over £330m in the summer, still score less than almost everyone; Richarlison has not played since August
facts: Sky says Spurs spent over £330m this summer yet only two Premier League sides scored fewer goals after 10 matches.
Richarlison rejected a move to Everton at the end of the summer window, has not played for the first team since August and is out of contract in the summer; Spurs want to find him a new club.
Eli Junior Kroupi was a summer target; Bournemouth would want a huge fee to sell in January.
background: Spurs won the Europa League in 2025, beating Manchester United in the final.

headline: Harry Kane wins the Ballon d'Or at 33, one of the oldest first-time winners
facts: Kane won his first men's Ballon d'Or at the London Palladium; ESPN's 11 Nov piece describes it as part of a fortnight of milestones, so the ceremony was roughly two weeks earlier.
He is the fourth-oldest first-time winner, at 33, and has 156 goals in 161 games for Bayern since a €120m move in August 2023.
He has 91 England goals and is closing on Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps.
background: Kane scored 280 goals in 435 games across 19 years at Tottenham but never broke Clive Allen's single-season club record of 49 goals.

headline: Fulham 1-1 Newcastle: Murphy's 80th-minute screamer cancelled out three minutes later, pressure on Jaissle grows
facts: Jacob Murphy scored from long range in the 80th minute and Rodrigo Muniz equalised for Fulham in the 83rd.
A stoppage-time save from Lukas Hornicek prevented a fifth Newcastle league defeat of the season.
After 10 games Newcastle are 12th with 12 points; Jaissle's side had been six points clear of Fulham in early October.
background: Jaissle previously managed Al Ahli, where he coached Ivan Toney, per Sky Sports.

headline: Everton knock Newcastle out of the Carabao Cup 3-1, then win again in the league four days later
facts: Everton won 3-1 in the Carabao Cup fourth round with goals from James Garner, Hayden Hackney and Thierno Barry, and face Fleetwood in the quarter-final.
The tie came after Newcastle had lost to Coventry and Aston Villa in the league, putting Jaissle under pressure.
Everton also beat Newcastle 1-0 in the league four days later with a Barry goal at St James' Park.
background: Everton have not won a trophy since the 1995 FA Cup.
footage_terms: Moyes Everton Carabao Cup quarter final

headline: Newcastle full-back Dedic stopped by police with a bow and arrows near a Newcastle reservoir
facts: A member of the public reported two men carrying a bow and arrows on a track by a reservoir near Harlow Hill, and several police units attended.
Dedic and a friend were stopped in a vehicle; police found they posed no danger, understood the bow to be for recreational use, seized it and said inquiries are ongoing.
The article is dated 6 Nov and refers to the incident on Wednesday, so 4 Nov is inferred; no Newcastle statement is quoted.
background: Dedic, 24, is a Bosnia and Herzegovina international who joined from Benfica in the summer for a reported £29.5m.

headline: Gordon grades his Barcelona start 7.5 out of 10, says he wants to be 'more selfish'
facts: Gordon left Newcastle for Barcelona this summer for an initial €70m and rates his start 7.5 out of 10, with three goals and four assists.
He went six games without a goal before scoring against Getafe, Galatasaray and Alaves.
England coach Tuchel said Gordon has reached another level; Gordon scored in England's World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina.
background: At Newcastle Gordon scored 16 times last season including 10 in the Champions League, after going from 25 January to 2 December 2025 without a league goal or assist.

headline: Bruno Guimaraes returns to St James' Park with Arsenal, who paid a reported £75m
facts: Arsenal signed Guimaraes for a reported £75m; he started slowly after an early-season injury but is now a first-choice midfielder.
Arteta said he is playing at a high level but wants more impact and more close-range goals, closer to Declan Rice's standard.
He faces Newcastle at St James' Park on Saturday 21 November (5:30pm); Arsenal are five points clear at the top, and Jaissle says his return will not be a distraction.
background: Guimaraes scored nine Premier League goals for Newcastle last season and 31 league goals in total for the club.

headline: Dan Burn called into England squad as Guehi withdraws injured
facts: Marc Guehi withdrew from Tuchel's squad after being substituted at half-time in Manchester City's loss to Nottingham Forest, ending a run of 15 straight England appearances.
Newcastle's Dan Burn replaced him for Nations League games against Croatia at Wembley and Spain.
Burn has 11 caps and last featured at the summer World Cup as a late substitute in the win over Mexico.
background: Guehi's withdrawal came after Manchester City lost to Nottingham Forest; England then played world champions Spain on Sunday 15 November.
footage_terms: Dan Burn England Mexico World Cup

headline: Newcastle's Lewis Hall completes five more first-half dribbles than Yamal in England's 3-2 win in Spain
facts: In the first half of England's 3-2 win over Spain in Madrid, Hall completed five dribbles, five more than Lamine Yamal.
Tuchel left him out of the summer World Cup squad, and England went with arguably only one specialist left-back.
Hall is 22, started as a midfielder in Chelsea's youth teams, and Berrada said United considered him but would not pay inflated prices.
background: Hall played well in Newcastle's home Champions League tie against Barcelona but was in the side that conceded seven in the away leg.

headline: Coventry hammer Newcastle 4-1, their first home Premier League win in 25 years
facts: Coventry scored through Rudoni (6' penalty), Cherif (48'), Simms (81') and Mfuni (86'); Sven Botman got Newcastle's goal in the 70th minute.
It was Coventry's first home Premier League victory in 25 years.
Newcastle had 67% possession and higher expected goals (1.84 to 1.43) but wasted chances.
background: Newcastle were 11th after the defeat, having started the season by drawing 2-2 with Bournemouth.
footage_terms: Coventry City first home win Premier League

headline: Jaissle wants a No. 9 and a No. 10 in January but cash is tight; Toney is admired
facts: Sky reports Newcastle lack an out-and-out No. 10, with Willock and Wissa both used there without being natural in the role.
Signing a nine and a ten looks unlikely unless Newcastle sell players; Jaissle also wants more experience after several senior players left in the summer.
Jaissle admires Ivan Toney, whom he managed at Al Ahli, but a move is seen as unlikely to fit the club's strategy of buying young.
background: Newcastle have won only one of their five home Premier League games this season.

headline: Aston Villa beat Man City 2-1 at Villa Park: Jackson brace, Donnarumma blunder
facts: Nicolas Jackson scored in the 6th and 60th minutes, with Erling Haaland equalising in the 52nd.
Commentary singled out an error by City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma on Jackson's second goal.
Villa have now beaten City at Villa Park four seasons in a row and moved into the top six, despite City having 63% possession and higher expected goals.
background: Per the match page, it was Villa's fifth win over City in seven league meetings.
footage_terms: Emery Villa Man City press conference

headline: Villa win 1-0 at Newcastle through Manzambi; Emery picks up his 100th Premier League win
facts: Johan Manzambi headed the only goal in the 36th minute at St James' Park.
Villa won consecutive league matches at St James' Park for the first time since 1957-58.
It was Unai Emery's 100th Premier League win as a manager; goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made key saves, including one late on.
background: Villa and Newcastle both finished the match on 8 points.

headline: Barcelona beat Villa 3-0 at Camp Nou, ending Villa's perfect Champions League start
facts: Lamine Yamal scored in the 7th minute and Raphinha added two more (52', 64') at Spotify Camp Nou.
Villa's perfect Champions League record ended; both teams have 9 points after four games.
Yamal became the competition's top teenage scorer, ahead of Kylian Mbappe, and Raphinha has 19 goals in 13 games this season.
background: Villa went into the match unbeaten in the Champions League league phase, level on 9 points with Barcelona after four games.

headline: Bournemouth knock Villa out of the Carabao Cup with a 3-0 win
facts: Amine Adli (7'), Lewis Cook (51') and Alvaro Rodriguez (69') scored at the Vitality Stadium in the fourth round.
Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made seven saves on target.
The page's shot map conflicts with the scorer list, so scorers and minutes should be rechecked against a match report.
background: Villa went out of the competition at the fourth-round stage, days before drawing 1-1 with Fulham in the league.
footage_terms: Bournemouth 3-0 Aston Villa Carabao Cup highlights

headline: Villa keeper Suzuki fumbles a corner into his own net as Fulham draw 1-1
facts: Nicolas Jackson scored in the 39th minute; Zion Suzuki then tried to parry an Alex Iwobi corner and the ball crossed the line in the 64th minute.
John McGinn hit the crossbar with a first-half penalty.
Fulham had higher expected goals (2.21 to 1.71) and Villa stayed ninth.
background: Sky's Ref Watch later asked whether Lammens fouled Suzuki before United's late equaliser at Old Trafford on 8 November.

headline: Onana signs a new Villa contract while recovering from a cruciate injury suffered at the World Cup
facts: Onana, 25, signed a new Villa contract while still recovering from a cruciate ligament injury that ended his World Cup with Belgium early.
He said the early rehab was hard, especially mentally, and that the club renewing his deal during recovery meant a lot.
Emery's preview says Onana is returning from injury and Villa are also offering extensions to Lindelof, Maatsen and George Hemmings.
background: Onana joined Villa from Everton in summer 2024 and credited Emery with the club's recent European success, including a Europa League title.

headline: Sky: Villa's biggest unfinished business is a new contract for Unai Emery
facts: Sky calls Villa's summer window a success, with high-profile departures replaced and a younger squad with all positions filled.
It says the main unfinished business is a new contract for Emery, which it rates above any signing.
ESPN's projection puts Villa 10th with 13 points but 13th at the end of the season because their underlying expected-goals numbers look weak.
background: Emery has won the Europa League with Villa and reached his 100th Premier League win as a manager on 17 October.
footage_terms: Unai Emery Aston Villa press conference
